title: CSV export and the resolver import
spec: EXPORT: full fidelity — title,year,kind,why,status,stars,queue_position,tmdb_id,imdb_id,added_at,watched_at,review — RFC4180 quoting, UTF-8, and it re-imports EXACTLY (round-trip test is the acceptance evidence). IMPORT IS A RESOLVER, NOT A LOADER: Evan has no existing list and will generate one with a chatbot, so input is loose — title required, everything else optional. Each row is searched against T-3; a review screen shows candidate matches WITH POSTERS side by side; ambiguous rows are disambiguated by hand; unmatched rows surface for manual search or discard and are NEVER silently dropped. Nothing is committed until the whole review is confirmed. A row carrying tmdb_id skips the search entirely — that is what makes an export round-trip. Import order becomes initial queue order. HIGH RISK: bulk writes into Evan's data — the commit must be atomic and a failed import must leave the DB untouched. ACCEPT: the README's exact starter CSV imports cleanly; a 40-row chatbot-generated file resolves with ambiguities surfaced not guessed; export-then-import is a no-op.

locate.evidence: LOCATE: /api/search (T-3) is the resolver's engine and already merges TMDB and IGDB; /api/details caches artwork; the add path in POST /api/titles (T-4) already does duplicate detection via the (source,source_id) unique index and gap-tolerant appending. serialise() (T-4/titles.py) already derives link/link_label. db.connection() (T-2) is a real transaction context that rolls back on any exception — AC7's atomicity comes from using ONE connection for the whole commit rather than the per-call execute() helper. RISKS: (1) export must map tmdb_id/imdb_id from the source/source_id pair, and a game has no tmdb_id — the column must be blank rather than carrying an IGDB id under a TMDB header; (2) Python's csv module needs newline='' or it doubles line endings on some platforms; (3) a chatbot CSV will arrive with a code fence, a BOM, or smart quotes, and the README tells Evan to paste raw output.

plan.evidence: PLAN: (1) GET /api/export.csv streaming the exact README columns; (2) POST /api/import/preview — parse, then resolve each row (tmdb_id short-circuit, else search) into matched / needs-choice / unmatched / duplicate buckets, writing NOTHING; (3) POST /api/import/commit taking the confirmed choices and inserting them all inside ONE transaction; (4) the import UI: paste or upload, a review screen with posters for the ambiguous rows, then commit; (5) export button. DECISIONS: preview and commit are separate endpoints so AC6 is structural rather than a promise; the commit uses a single connection so a failure anywhere rolls the whole thing back; a leading BOM and a wrapping code fence are stripped on parse because the README tells Evan to paste chatbot output and that is what chatbot output looks like; and an existing seen row is reported as a duplicate rather than updated, so an import can never quietly drag something back out of the archive.

auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED — THREE defects, all in this ticket's own design, all fixed and re-verified. (1) THE EXPORT COULD NOT ROUND-TRIP A GAME: the published columns had tmdb_id but no igdb_id, so a game exported with no id at all and had to be re-resolved by search on the way back — approximate, not exact, and a re-resolve can land elsewhere. Added igdb_id and updated README.md, which is the contract Evan was told to rely on; his chatbot prompt format is untouched. (2) THE RESOLVER NEARLY IMPORTED A VIDEO GAME AS AN ANIME: there is a 1998 Cowboy Bebop GAME as well as the 1998 anime, and they scored 168 to 140 — 28 apart, close enough that any weight change flips it, on a row that explicitly said 'anime'. Fixed by making a declared kind a FILTER rather than a preference: candidates of another kind are not answers to that row. (3) THE BUTTON PROMISED A NUMBER THE COMMIT WOULD NOT DELIVER: hand-picking a candidate marked the row ready without re-checking it against the list, so the UI said 'Import 3' and the commit did 2 — the commit was right, the promise was wrong. Preview now returns the existing key set and picking a duplicate flips the row immediately; re-verified end to end, the promise now matches the result. Design decisions standing: preview and commit are separate endpoints so 'nothing is written until you confirm' is structural; all network fetches happen BEFORE the transaction opens so no upstream request holds a write lock; and a duplicate is reported rather than updated.
